name: Pakiri Beach
land: Council reserve / beach + private farmland access
access: Pakiri Rd north of Leigh, ~1 h 30 from CBD. Park at the beach access; the dunes and farmland behind are private.
best: Twenty kilometres of empty white sand with dunes and no one on it. The best 'alone' flying in the region.
hazards: Private farmland behind the beach (no crossing without permission), surf and rips, no phone coverage, very exposed to wind.
note: Airspace is clean - 10.9 km from Omaha Flats. Take water, tell someone where you are, and don't stray onto the farm.

name: Leigh / Leigh Harbour
access: Leigh village, ~70 min from CBD. Harbour launch at the wharf end, beach at the surf side.
best: Two completely different looks in one village: sheltered harbour with boats and bush, and open surf beach with cliffs north.
hazards: Charter boats and divers at the harbour, swimmers at the beach, the Leigh cemetery is a no-fly polygon inside the village.
note: 7.3 km from Omaha Flats so no aerodrome consent needed. Log the flight on AirShare.

name: Mahurangi West / Opahi Bay
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Mahurangi West Rd off SH1, ~45 min from CBD. Park at Opahi Bay or Sullivan's Bay.
best: Sheltered harbour bays, bush headlands, tidal flats and boats - classic Mahurangi postcard, almost nobody there.
hazards: Tide (the flats are mud at low water), regional park permit conditions, narrow gravel road.
note: Mahurangi is not on the banned list, so a regional-park drone permit is available through council. Apply first.

name: Algies Bay
access: Algies Bay Rd, ~1 h from CBD. Beach reserve with parking.
best: Quiet bay, moorings, bush-clad points and Kawau Island across the water - good long-range line of sight.
hazards: Moorings and dinghies, swimmers in summer, tide
note: No permit needed. 8 km from Warkworth heliport, so airspace is clean. Dawn is flat calm.

name: Sandspit
access: Sandspit Rd, ~55 min from CBD. Marina at the end of the road.
best: Estuary, marina masts, sandspit and the Matakana river mouth - lots of interesting structure to fly.
hazards: Marina is private property (don't launch from the pontoons), ferry and boat traffic, estuary birds.
note: 5.9 km from Omaha Flats - just outside the 4 km ring. Launch from the reserve, not the marina.

name: Omaha Beach
access: Omaha Dr, ~65 min from CBD.
best: White sand, surf, dunes and the inlet - the most photogenic beach in the north.
hazards: Inside the Omaha Flats aerodrome 4 km ring: needs a Part 101 certificate and aerodrome operator consent. Also busy in summer.
note: Legal only with a qualification and consent; without it, drive 10 minutes to Leigh instead. Pin is the main beach access; the old pin was 500 m up the beach.

name: Wenderholm Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Wenderholm off SH1 just north of Puhoi, ~45 min from CBD.
best: Bush, beach and the Puhoi river mouth - a compact, sheltered spot with great light in the evening.
hazards: Permit conditions, popular picnic spot on weekends, estuary birds, no flying over the campground when occupied.
note: Regional park permit required. One of the few north parks where the permit is actually worth the paperwork.

name: Puhoi
access: Puhoi village off SH1, ~40 min from CBD. Park at the domain or the pub.
best: River, bush valley, the old stone church and the bridge - tight, scenic flying with real character.
hazards: Kayak traffic on the river in summer, dense bush limits LOS, narrow valley wind.
note: No permit. Fly the river corridor early; the valley is shaded and calm before 9am.

name: Waiwera
access: Waiwera off SH1, ~40 min from CBD.
best: Small beach at the mouth of the Waiwera river, cliffs either side, easy parking off the highway.
hazards: Highway noise and traffic, swimmers, small beach so keep clear of people.
note: No permit. Quick stop on the way north rather than a destination. Pin is the river-mouth beach.

name: Manly / Big Manly Beach
access: Manly, Whangaparaoa, ~45 min from CBD.
best: Sheltered beach with a headland at each end and Whangaparaoa harbour behind - good for smooth coastal passes.
hazards: Swimmers and boat ramp traffic in summer, residential overlooks.
note: No permit. Clean airspace, 10 km from North Shore aerodrome. Pin is the beach frontage at Big Manly.

name: Stanmore Bay
access: Stanmore Bay Rd, Whangaparaoa, ~45 min from CBD.
best: Long beach, rocks at the northern end and a big open park behind - easy launch with room to breathe.
hazards: Busy in summer, sports fields and playground, swimmers.
note: No permit. The northern rocks are the interesting end. The old pin was 1 km south on Scott Road, away from the bay. Pin is the northern end of the beach by the boat ramp; the old pin was 650 m inland in the housing.

name: Tindalls Beach
access: Tindalls Beach Rd, Whangaparaoa, ~45 min from CBD.
best: Small sheltered bay with a tidal inlet - quiet, pretty, limited space.
hazards: Residential bay with houses close on both sides, swimmers, small launch area.
note: No permit, but it's a small stage - good for a 30-minute session, not a full day.

name: Hatfields Beach
access: Hatfields Beach off SH1, ~40 min from CBD.
best: Quiet beach with a rocky northern end and the Orewa estuary behind - the overflow option when Orewa is packed.
hazards: Highway-adjacent, small parking, shorebirds at the estuary.
note: No permit. Pairs with Orewa or Waiwera in one run. 1 km inland. Pin is on the sand at the northern end of the beach.

name: Orewa Beach
access: Orewa, ~35 min from CBD. Beach car parks along Orewa Beach Rd.
best: Three kilometres of beach, estuary mouth and the Whangaparaoa headland in the distance - the easiest big-stage beach in the north.
hazards: Busiest beach in the north: swimmers, kite surfers, events, estuary shorebirds.
note: No permit, clean airspace, but you'll be flying around people. Dawn or a weekday evening.

name: Browns Bay
access: Browns Bay, ~22 min from CBD.
best: Beach, reef at low tide and the islands offshore - the best North Shore option if you're not certificated.
hazards: Inside Whenuapai CTR but within the Whangaparaoa VFR transit lane: no ATC authorisation needed in daylight, but you must be on the ground before dark.
note: This one is a daylight-only exception. The transit lane is uncontrolled during daylight hours - night ops need ATC authorisation. Busy beach in summer.

name: Long Bay
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT + ATC authorisation
access: Long Bay, ~30 min from CBD.
best: Long sandy beach, cliffs and the regional park headland at the northern end.
hazards: Inside the Whenuapai CTR (outside the transit lane) and a regional park - two separate permissions.
note: Not worth it when Browns Bay is 4 km south and needs neither. Skip unless you're doing the paperwork anyway.

name: Devonport / North Head
land: Council reserve + DOC historic reserve (North Head)
access: Devonport, 20 min from CBD by ferry or 30 by road.
best: The best city skyline and harbour shot in Auckland - cliffs, gun emplacements, Rangitoto and the CBD across the water.
hazards: Inside the Mechanics Bay and Auckland Harbour 4 km rings, plus North Shore Hospital. North Head itself is DOC land needing a separate concession.
note: Sits in the Northern Automatic Authorisation Area: automatic approval ONLY with a Part 101 qualification from a Part 141 provider plus an observer. Without the cert, no.

name: Narrow Neck Beach
access: Narrow Neck Beach, off Old Lake Rd, Devonport.
best: Long east-facing beach with the harbour and Rangitoto in frame; sheltered in a westerly.
hazards: Swimmers, paddleboarders, ferry wakes, cliff at the north end.
note: The best Devonport beach that still sits outside the harbour control zone.

name: Little Manly Beach
access: Little Manly Beach, off Ngaio St, Manly.
best: Small sheltered bay with rocks and a wharf — flat water in most conditions.
hazards: Wharf users, moored boats, ferry traffic from Gulf Harbour.
note: Shelter when the east-coast beaches are blown out.

name: Matakatia Bay
access: Matakatia Beach, off Matakatia Pde.
best: Quiet residential bay with a long low-tide sandbar and clear water.
hazards: Residents' moorings, low-tide mud, narrow launch at high tide.
note: A locals-only feel; keep the noise down and stay off the sandbar at low tide.

name: Arkles Bay Beach
access: Arkles Bay Beach, off Arkles Strand.
best: Sheltered swimming beach with a boat ramp and a rocky point at the north end.
hazards: Boat ramp traffic in summer, swimmers, kayaks.
note: The ramp makes carrying gear easy; the same ramp makes it busy on a Saturday morning.

name: Army Bay
access: Army Bay, end of Whangaparaoa Rd; car park by the beach.
best: Wide bay with a long beach, rocky ends and open water toward Tiritiri Matangi.
hazards: Boat traffic to Gulf Harbour, divers in summer, wind funnelling down the peninsula.
note: The pick of the Whangaparaoa bays for open-water lines.

name: Shakespear Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Shakespear Regional Park, end of Whangaparaoa Rd; gate opens 6am.
best: Cliffs, farmland and three bays — the most varied flying on the peninsula.
hazards: Stock, cliff updraughts, heavy weekend visitation, permit conditions.
note: Needs a regional park permit; the northern cliffs are the reason to bother.

name: Scandrett Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Scandrett Regional Park, off Scandrett Rd, Mahurangi East.
best: Rolling coastal farmland above the Mahurangi harbour — huge sightlines, nobody around.
hazards: Stock, steep drops to the water, gravel road in, permit conditions.
note: The quietest regional park in the north; pair it with a Mahurangi West trip.

name: Ti Point
access: Ti Point Rd, off Leigh Rd; small reserve at the end.
best: Rocky coast and bush at the mouth of the Matakana river — quiet and unusual.
hazards: Private land either side, rocky shore, tide.
note: Stay on the reserve — the surrounding blocks are private.

name: Te Arai Beach
access: Te Arai Point Rd, off Pakiri Rd; gravel car park at the point.
best: Long empty surf beach, dunes and forestry blocks — the wildest flying in the region.
hazards: Surf and rips, no patrols, forestry operations, soft sand, no phone coverage.
note: An hour and a half from the city and worth every minute of it.
